action_items: None blocking. Consider addressing the React console warning by fixing the runtime instrumentation wrapper OR moving '{d.name} ({d.count})' into a single text expression (already the case in source, so this looks purely tool-side).

OPTIONAL: The frontend surfaces backend upload errors as just the raw 'detail' string (e.g. 'HTTP 500'). Consider mapping known status codes (413/415/400) to more human-friendly messages in NotificationEmailView.onImport catch branch.

OPTIONAL: The `email` uniqueness constraint means uploading an xlsx with duplicate emails would fail the bulk insert mid-flight after delete_many wiped the collection — leaving the roster in a partial state. Consider (a) deduping in parse_employees_xlsx, or (b) using a transaction / temp collection swap for atomicity.
critical_code_review_comments: BUG FIXED: /app/backend/employees.py::replace_all_employees was creating a NON-unique index on `email` while bootstrap_employees_if_empty created a UNIQUE index. Same index name, different options -> MongoDB IndexKeySpecsConflict -> 500 on every roster re-upload. Fixed by matching unique=True in both call sites. Root cause: the same index needs the same options everywhere; consider factoring _ensure_indexes(db) into a single helper called by both bootstrap and replace to prevent drift.

The employees module writes email lower-cased on parse (good) but does NOT dedupe within the same file, so an .xlsx with two rows sharing the same email will now (post-fix) raise BulkWriteError after the collection has already been wiped. Add `rows = list({r['email']: r for r in rows}.values())` in replace_all_employees or parse_employees_xlsx to dedupe.

server.py::import_employees does not catch pymongo.errors.BulkWriteError or DuplicateKeyError. A user uploading a file with duplicate emails would today receive a raw 500. Wrap `await replace_all_employees(...)` in try/except and translate to 409.

NotificationEmailView.js hard-codes reading the CSRF cookie via a regex: `(document.cookie.match(/hrcert_csrf=([^;]+)/) || [])[1]`. All other state-changing calls use apiFetch which likely already adds the header. Consider routing this multipart POST through the same helper (or a variant that skips Content-Type auto-setting) rather than duplicating the CSRF-cookie parsing logic.

employees.py::list_employees uses `department.lower() != 'all'` to allow an 'all' sentinel, but the frontend never sends 'all' (it sends empty string -> no query param). Either wire the FE 'All' shortcut, or drop the dead branch.

server.py is now ~890 lines — well past the 700-line guideline. Splitting into routers/{auth,certificate,offer,offer_email,offer_appointment,ack,employees,history}.py is overdue; each is self-contained.

Notification Email textarea `notif-bcc` is readOnly but is still an <textarea>; a keyboard user tabbing into it can't tell it's read-only from a screen reader (no aria-readonly). Add aria-readonly="true" or convert to a <div role="textbox">.

rca of the issue: BUG (fixed): POST /api/employees/import returned 500 on every re-upload. Root cause: MongoDB rejects create_index(name=X, options=Y1) when an index with the same auto-generated name X already exists with different options Y2. bootstrap_employees_if_empty (employees.py:122) created `email_1` with unique=True on first boot, but replace_all_employees (employees.py:135) tried to create the same-named index with unique=False. Mongo error: IndexKeySpecsConflict, code 86, propagated as 500. Reproduction: POST /api/employees/import <seed.xlsx>  →  500 Internal Server Error; check backend logs for 'existing index has the same name'. Fix: change employees.py:135 to `await db.employees.create_index('email', unique=True)`. Verified: after fix, /api/employees/import returns 200 {'ok': true, 'inserted': 52} and the FE banner shows 'Roster replaced — 52 employees imported.'.
